'''Yamato no Nagaoka''' (やまと の ながおか) was a {{ill|Nara period|en|Nara period|qid=Q189178|lt=Nara period}} [[:en:Japanese nobility|Japanese nobility]] and [[Myōbōdō|legal scholar]]. His initial name was '''Kotohito''' (小東人). He bore the [[kabane]] [[Imiki]] but later changed to [[Sukune]]. His {{ill|Rank|en|Rank|qid=Q4120621|lt=Rank}} was [[Senior Fourth Rank|Senior Fourth Rank, Lower]], and he served as [[Kuni no miyatsuko]] of {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}}.

== Career ==
From a young age, Nagaoka had a passion for the study of penal law and was skilled in [[Kidentō|literary composition]]<ref name="a">''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'', entry for the 3rd year of [[Shingo Keiun]], [[October 29 (lunar calendar)|October 29]]</ref>. In [[Reiki 2]] (716), he accompanied the [[:en:Kentōshi|Kentōshi]] mission to [[:en:Tang China|Tang China]] as a student. During his time in Tang, he clarified many previously unresolved issues. Upon his return, Nagaoka became a leading authority on [[Myōbōdō|law]], with students seeking his teachings. In [[Yōrō 6]] (722), he was awarded four chō of {{ill|Kuden|en|kuden|qid=Q629640|lt=kuden}} for his contributions to the compilation of the ''{{ill|Yōrō Code|en|Yōrō Code|qid=Q2575743|lt=Yōrō Code}}''. At the time, he held the Rank of [[Junior Sixth Rank, Upper]].

In [[Tenpyō 9]] (737), following a divine oracle, he and his relative Mizumori were granted the [[kabane]] Sukune, while other clan members were renamed to [[Muraji]]. Concurrently, Nagaoka was promoted from [[Senior Sixth Rank, Upper]] to [[Junior Fifth Rank, Lower]] (Outer) and received 20 bolts of {{ill|Aya|en|aya|qid=Q2819612|lt=aya}} cloth. In [[Tenpyō 10]] (738), he was appointed as {{ill|Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|es|Ministerio de Justicia (Japón)|fa|وزارت دادگستری (ژاپن پیشامدرن)|ff|Ministry of Justice (pre-modern Japan)|fr|Gyōbu-shō|ja|刑部省|vi|Hình Bộ Tỉnh (Nhật Bản)|zh|刑部省|qid=Q6867320|lt=Gyōbu Shōbu}}. Despite being implicated in the [[:en:Fujiwara no Hirotsugu Rebellion|Fujiwara no Hirotsugu Rebellion]] in [[Tenpyō 13]] (741) and exiled, he was later pardoned. By [[Tenpyō 16]] (744), he served as assistant to the {{ill|Saikaidō|en|Saikaidō|qid=Q1334003|lt=Saikaidō Inspector}}, later becoming [[Settsu no Suke]] in [[Tenpyō 18]] (746), and was promoted to [[Junior Fifth Rank, Lower]] (Inner) in [[Tenpyō 19]] (747).

During the reigns of {{ill|Empress Kōken|en|Empress Kōken|qid=Q232955|lt=Empress Kōken}} and {{ill|Emperor Junnin|en|Emperor Junnin|qid=Q329713|lt=Emperor Junnin}}, he steadily advanced: [[Junior Fifth Rank, Upper]] in [[Tenpyō Shōhō 2]] (750), [[Senior Fifth Rank, Lower]] in [[Tenpyō Shōhō 3]] (751), [[Senior Fifth Rank, Upper]] in [[Tenpyō Shōhō 9]] (757), and [[Junior Fourth Rank, Lower]] in [[Tenpyō Hōji 7]] (763). He held various positions, including [[Suruga no Kami]], [[Shibi Chūtai|Shibi Daichū]], [[Minbushō|Minbu Daisuke]], [[Kyōshiki|Sakyō Daibu]], and {{ill|Kawachi Province|be|Каваты (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Kawachi|ckb|پارێزگای کاواچی|cs|Provincie Kawači|de|Provinz Kawachi|es|Provincia de Kawachi|fa|ولایت کاواچی|fr|Province de Kawachi|gl|Provincia de Kawachi|hak|Kawachi-koet|id|Provinsi Kawachi|it|Kawachi (provincia)|ja|河内国|ko|가와치국|lt|Kavačio žemė|nl|Kawachi (provincie)|pt|Província de Kawachi|ru|Кавати (провинция)|simple|Kawachi Province|sk|Kawači (provincia)|sr|Провинција Кавачи|tr|Kawachi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Каваті|zh|河內國|zh_min_nan|Kawati-kok|zh_yue|河內國|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi no Kami}}. However, he was criticized for his lack of benevolence in governance, leading to suffering among his subordinates and the populace<ref name="a" />. In [[Tenpyō Hōji 8]] (764), he became [[Ukyo Daibu]], but soon retired due to old age.

In [[Shingo Keiun 2]] (768), during a New Year’s banquet, he was granted special permission to attend court. Empress [[Kōken|Shōtoku]] was impressed by his vitality and rich hair at the age of 80. When asked his age, he replied, prompting the empress to write his promotion certificate herself, raising him to [[Senior Fourth Rank, Lower]]. Nagaoka passed away on [[Shingo Keiun 3]], [[October 29 (lunar calendar)|October 29]] (December 1, 769), at 81. His final Rank was [[Kuni no miyatsuko|Yamato Kuni no miyatsuko]], Senior Fourth Rank, Lower.

He was one of the authors of the ''[[Santei Ritsuryō]]'', established in [[Shingo Keiun 3]] (769) and implemented in [[Enryaku 10]] (791), alongside [[Kibi no Makibi]].
